page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 7H12 cores running at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.g6a.large sits in the lower performance tiers for intensive computational tasks. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests register scores of 766.59, placing the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth performance is similarly constrained, with small-block cached reads reaching 83.78 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads and writes registering at 23.06 GB/sec and 15.78 GB/sec respectively. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression shows average performance at 9.2 GB/sec, while gzip compression is weak at 23.75 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but lower benchmark scores, the instance offers an entry-level dedicated resource profile. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations fall into the bottom 10%, indicating that this instance is not suited for high-throughput database workloads. Static web serving throughput is also low at 2.03 GB/sec. The instance is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, or low-intensity background tasks where dedicated CPU cores are required but raw processing speed is not critical.
